title: Slide 1 · Checking a language model’s claims
question: C1’s pickup record says North Desk and C2’s says South Desk. A message about C1 cites the C2 record. What would you inspect before trusting the message?
answer: Match the item, relationship and location in the cited record to the message. A real pickup record can still be the wrong source if it describes C2.

title: Slide 2 · A fluent sentence can contain two claims
question: In the sample reply, which claim follows from the prompt’s records and which would require more evidence?
answer: D8 gives C1’s pickup desk. H3 gives a deadline for C2, so the time for C1 remains unknown. A supported reply could say, “Collect C1 at West Desk [D8]. I do not have a pickup deadline for C1.”

title: Slide 3 · Find support at the level of one claim
question: Would searching only for the word “noon” catch the item mix-up?
answer: No. H3 contains “noon” but its item is C2. A claim about C1 needs evidence about C1.

title: Slide 4 · Tell a contradiction from a gap
question: What changes if several desks can serve C1 and D8 lists just one of them?
answer: West Desk remains supported. East Desk becomes unknown unless another record excludes it. One listed option no longer rules out other options.

title: Slide 5 · Make time part of the claim
question: A user forwards Monday’s answer without the date. Why should Tuesday’s desk avoid reusing it?
answer: Monday’s record establishes the location only for Monday. Tuesday’s record gives East Desk. Omitting the day hides which claim the citation supports.

title: Slide 6 · Check the camera in each proposed claim
question: Replace this line: "H3": ("C2", "pickup_deadline", "noon")} with: "H3": ("C1", "pickup_deadline", "noon")} What will print?
answer:
pickup_at D8
pickup_deadline H3
Changing the camera in H3 makes the item, relationship and value all agree with the deadline claim.

title: Slide 8 · From this module to the next
question: Ava verifies that C1 is available now. A proposed sequence reserves it for Bo and then promises Ava she can reserve it too. Why check the second step again?
answer: The first action can change availability. A claim that was supported before Bo’s reservation may no longer hold when Ava’s step is reached.

title: Office hours · Where does the language model actually run in these examples?
question: Where does the language model actually run in these examples?
answer: The first example builds the prompt you could give an LLM. The lesson then supplies a sample draft and its individual claims. The Python cells run the evidence checks. Holding the draft fixed lets two students inspect the same mistake. In a working system, a model could receive the question and retrieved passages and produce the draft.

title: Office hours · Can a checker always decide support by comparing strings?
question: Can a checker always decide support by comparing strings?
answer: Our records use agreed names, so equality is enough for these examples. Real sources might say “collect” where a draft says “pick up”. Someone must map those expressions to the same meaning and check details such as item and date before trusting the match.

title: Exercise 1
question: Split “Mia may collect T2 at Room 4 tomorrow without showing ID” into claims. Which one needs policy evidence?
answer: Check Mia’s permission to collect T2 tomorrow, T2’s pickup room tomorrow, and whether the relevant policy permits collection without ID. The last claim requires an applicable ID policy, and the first may also require checking eligibility rules.

title: Exercise 2
question: There is exactly one current due date per loan. L2 lists Friday for Ava’s C1 loan. L3 lists Thursday for Ben’s C2 loan. Classify “Ava’s C1 is due Thursday” and “Ava owes a late fee.”
answer: The Thursday due-date claim is contradicted by Ava’s Friday date in L2. The fee claim is unknown. Neither record gives a fee assessment, and L3 belongs to a different loan.

title: Exercise 3
question: A correct answer says “Room 4” but cites an old record for Room 1. Would a check that compares only the answer text to an answer key catch the defect? Design a stronger check.
answer: A text-only check could accept Room 4. Fetch the cited ID and compare its item, relation, date and value with the claim. The old Room 1 record fails that check. Supply the current Room 4 record if available.

title: Lab case 1 · A supported location
question: Which record supports this claim?
answer: D8 matches the camera, location and day. D9 is about another camera.

title: Lab case 2 · A contradicted location
question: Which verdict follows, and why?
answer: Contradicted. With one desk for that camera and day, the current West Desk assignment excludes East Desk.

title: Lab case 3 · A plausible deadline
question: Which part can you publish?
answer: West Desk for C1 on Monday is supported by D8. The noon deadline for C1 is unknown. H3 concerns C2.
